research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines the prevalence of coronavirus infection in wild bat populations globally from 1996-2019, investigating how methodological factors (sample type, sampling design, use of euthanasia), spatiotemporal variables, and taxonomic factors influence virus detection rates to inform future surveillance strategies.

comparison: Control conditions (waitlist, treatment as usual, or no intervention)
intervention: Creative arts-based interventions (music, dance, visual art, drama, and movement therapy)
outcome: PTSD symptom severity measured by validated pre-post PTSD outcome measures
population: Children and adolescents aged 3-18 years with diagnosed PTSD or trauma-related symptoms
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether creative arts-based interventions (including music, dance, visual art, and drama) are effective in reducing PTSD symptoms among children and adolescents aged 3-18 years with diagnosed PTSD or trauma-related symptoms compared to control conditions, with particular attention to whether these interventions are more effective in non-Western populations than in Western populations.

comparison: Traditional statistical perspectives and non-computational approaches to studying interpersonal psychopathology
exposure: Application of computational modeling approaches (Bayesian modeling, machine learning, dynamical systems modeling, reinforcement learning) to study interpersonal dynamics
outcome: Validity, performance metrics, and transparency of computational models; identification of interpersonal disruptions (rigid social learning, hypo/hyper-mentalizing, polarized relational dynamics); adoption of open science practices
population: Individuals with mental health conditions including mood disorders, autism spectrum disorder, psychotic conditions, and personality disorders
research_question: This systematic review evaluates the utility and validity of computational modeling approaches (including Bayesian modeling, machine learning, dynamical systems modeling, and reinforcement learning) in investigating interpersonal dynamics in psychopathology, examining whether these methods can provide theoretically notable and methodologically reliable insights about social and relational disruptions across various mental health conditions.

comparison: Treatment as usual (TAU), antidepressant medication (ADM), or evaluation-only control
intervention: Psychological interventions including cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT), continuation cognitive therapy (C-CT), and preventive cognitive therapy (PCT)
outcome: Depression relapse risk over 12 months (measured by hazard ratio for time to relapse)
population: Adults with remitted major depressive disorder (previously depressed patients who achieved remission)
research_question: This individual participant data meta-analysis investigates whether psychological interventions (including cognitive behavioral therapy, mindfulness-based cognitive therapy, continuation cognitive therapy, and preventive cognitive therapy) are effective in preventing depression relapse in patients with remitted major depressive disorder compared to treatment as usual, antidepressant medication, or evaluation-only control, and identifies which patient subgroups benefit most from these interventions.

comparison: Various control conditions including neutral states (waiting, doing nothing), positive affect states (fun, excitement, interest, engagement), and negative affect states (anger, anxiety, sadness)
exposure: Boredom (state or trait, measured via self-report scales or experimentally induced)
outcome: Arousal levels measured via self-report (sleepiness, restlessness) and physiological indicators (heart rate, heart rate variability, cortisol levels, electrodermal activity, blood pressure, respiration rate)
population: Human, non-clinical participants
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the relationship between boredom and physiological/self-reported arousal in human non-clinical participants, examining whether boredom is associated with higher or lower arousal levels compared to various control conditions, and identifying moderators that explain heterogeneity in findings across correlational and experimental studies.

comparison: Expected survival of age- and sex-matched individuals from the general population (reference population without cancer)
exposure: Diagnosis of uveal melanoma
outcome: Long-term relative survival rates (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30-year relative survival)
population: Patients with uveal melanoma (choroidal or ciliary body melanomas)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to determine the long-term relative survival rates in patients with uveal melanoma, specifically estimating the proportion of patients who ultimately succumb to their disease over 5 to 30 years of follow-up, compared to the expected survival of age- and sex-matched individuals from the general population.

comparison: HIV-negative pregnant women
exposure: Maternal HIV infection and antiretroviral drug regimens (no ARVs, zidovudine monotherapy, combination antiretroviral therapy initiated antenatally or preconception)
outcome: Adverse perinatal outcomes including preterm birth (PTB), low birthweight (LBW), and small for gestational age (SGA)
population: Pregnant women living with HIV (WLHIV) in sub-Saharan Africa
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to determine the burden of adverse perinatal outcomes (preterm birth, low birthweight, and small for gestational age) attributable to maternal HIV infection and different antiretroviral drug regimens among pregnant women living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa between 1990 and 2020, compared to HIV-negative women.

comparison: Standard care (diet and lifestyle advice, home blood glucose monitoring, clinic reviews, with conventional treatment escalation pathway)
intervention: Personalized diet and lifestyle interventions, and pharmacological treatments (metformin, sulphonylureas, insulin) based on precision markers
outcome: Achievement of glucose targets, requirement for treatment escalation to pharmacological therapy, maternal outcomes, and neonatal outcomes
population: Pregnant women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates which patient-level characteristics serve as precision markers for predicting responses to personalized diet and lifestyle interventions, as well as the requirement for escalation from lifestyle management to pharmacological treatment (metformin, sulphonylureas, or insulin) in women with gestational diabetes mellitus, compared to standard care approaches.

comparison: Having personality change goals without intervention (non-intervention studies)
intervention: Volitional personality change (VPC) interventions designed to facilitate self-directed personality trait changes
outcome: Personality trait changes in the direction of personal change goals, persistence of changes during follow-up, and associated changes in well-being
population: General population with desires or goals to change their personality traits
research_question: This systematic review examines whether volitional personality change (VPC) interventions are effective in promoting desired personality trait changes in individuals who have goals to change their personality, compared to having change goals without intervention, and whether these changes persist over time and relate to other outcomes such as well-being.

comparison: Full modified Jones criteria including complete laboratory investigations and echocardiography at national referral hospitals
exposure: Simplified diagnostic algorithms for acute rheumatic fever (including clinical-only algorithms at community health centre-level, algorithms with 12-lead ECG and simple laboratory investigations at district-level, and modified Jones criteria without echocardiography)
outcome: Diagnostic test accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, AUC) for acute rheumatic fever diagnosis and progression to rheumatic heart disease
population: Children, adolescents, and adults with suspected acute rheumatic fever in high-prevalence areas (low to middle-income countries)
research_question: This systematic review evaluates the diagnostic test accuracy of simplified algorithms for diagnosing acute rheumatic fever compared to the 2015 modified Jones criteria among children, adolescents, and adults with suspected acute rheumatic fever, and assesses the impact of different diagnostic criteria on the development of rheumatic heart disease.

comparison: Standard care or no intervention (as modeled in decision analytic frameworks)
intervention: Cardiovascular disease prevention interventions (primordial, primary, and secondary prevention strategies)
outcome: Health outcomes (disability-adjusted life years, mortality), economic outcomes (cost-effectiveness), and equity impacts of CVD prevention interventions
population: Adult populations in sub-Saharan Africa at risk for or with cardiovascular disease
research_question: This systematic review examines how decision analytic models have been applied to evaluate cardiovascular disease prevention interventions in sub-Saharan Africa, assessing the types of prevention strategies modeled (primordial, primary, and secondary), the modeling methods used, the incorporation of equity dimensions, and the quality of existing models to identify gaps for future research.

comparison: Placebo
intervention: Disease-modifying therapies, primarily immunomodulatory agents (including teplizumab and other immunotherapies) and therapies targeting beta cell health and function
outcome: Prevention or delay of clinical type 1 diabetes onset, preservation of endogenous insulin production (measured by C-peptide levels), beta cell function, and identification of features linked to treatment response (age, beta cell function measures, immune phenotypes)
population: Individuals at increased risk for type 1 diabetes (pre-clinical stages) and individuals with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes
research_question: This systematic review examines whether disease-modifying therapies (primarily immunotherapies) can prevent or delay the onset of type 1 diabetes in at-risk individuals or preserve beta cell function in newly diagnosed patients, and identifies individual characteristics (such as age, beta cell function measures, and immune phenotypes) that are linked to treatment response to inform precision medicine approaches.

comparison: Absence or lower levels of risk factor exposure; models and findings from United States and European populations
exposure: Multiple risk factors including demographics (age, gender), health status (cardiometabolic diseases), mental health symptoms, lifestyle factors (sleep problems, alcohol consumption, physical activity), and social determinants of health (education, socioeconomic status)
outcome: Cognition (cognitive abilities including attention, problem-solving, learning, and memory) and functional ability (personal activities of daily living and instrumental skills)
population: Aging populations in Latin American countries (n = 146,000 participants)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the risk factors associated with healthy aging, specifically examining how demographics, health status, mental health, lifestyle factors, and social determinants of health influence cognition and functional ability in aging populations across Latin American countries, compared to models developed in the United States and Europe.

comparison: Untreated control or sham groups (healthy animals or disease model animals without RASI treatment)
intervention: Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASIs), including angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEIs) and angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs)
outcome: Tissue ACE2 mRNA and protein expression levels in the heart, kidneys, lungs, and other organs
population: Healthy animals and animal models of human diseases (including cardiovascular disease, hypertension, and acute lung injury models)
research_question: This systematic review investigates whether renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASIs), including angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEIs) and angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), cause overexpression of angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) in tissues of healthy animals and animal models of human diseases compared to control or sham groups.

comparison: Normal sleep duration and absence of insomnia symptoms
exposure: Habitual sleep duration (short sleep ≤6 hours, long sleep) and insomnia symptoms (sleep continuity disturbance, early-morning awakening, difficulty falling asleep, combined insomnia symptoms)
outcome: Incidence of hypertension (relative risk of developing hypertension)
population: Adults from prospective cohort studies with at least 1-year follow-up duration
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether habitual sleep duration (short or long) and insomnia symptoms (including sleep continuity disturbance, early-morning awakening, difficulty falling asleep, and combined symptoms) are associated with an increased risk of hypertension incidence in adults.

comparison: Placebo
intervention: Anti-cytokine treatment (cytokine modulators including anti-TNF drugs such as adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab, and tocilizumab)
outcome: Depressive symptoms (measured as secondary outcomes in clinical trials)
population: Patients with chronic inflammatory conditions (such as rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis) with depressive symptoms
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether anti-cytokine treatment (cytokine modulators including monoclonal antibodies and cytokine inhibitors) improves depressive symptoms in patients with chronic inflammatory conditions compared to placebo, and examines whether the antidepressant effect is related to improvement in physical illness, baseline depression severity, sex, or age.

comparison: Lowest adherence category to healthy dietary patterns
exposure: Adherence to healthy dietary patterns measured by predefined diet quality indices (Mediterranean diet score, Healthy Eating Index, Alternative Healthy Eating Index, Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension, Dietary Inflammatory Index)
outcome: Depressive symptoms and clinical depression incidence
population: General adult population from observational studies
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether adherence to healthy dietary patterns, measured using predefined diet quality indices such as the Mediterranean diet, Healthy Eating Index, Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension, and Dietary Inflammatory Index, is associated with reduced risk of depressive symptoms and clinical depression in the general population.

comparison: Healthy controls
exposure: Neuroeconomic gameplay paradigms (Game Theory-based social decision-making tasks)
outcome: Social decision-making behavior, brain activity patterns in regions associated with social information processing (anterior insula, orbitofrontal cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, temporoparietal junction), reward sensitivity, and integration of social and cognitive information
population: Individuals with Axis 1 psychiatric disorders
research_question: This review examines how neuroeconomic gameplay paradigms can be used to measure social decision-making abnormalities in individuals with Axis 1 psychiatric disorders, investigating behavioral and neuroimaging differences compared to healthy controls, with the aim of identifying biomarkers aligned with Research Domain Criteria (RDoC) constructs.

comparison: Less intensive systolic blood pressure control (≥130 mmHg)
intervention: Intensive systolic blood pressure control targeting <130 mmHg
outcome: Composite cardiovascular events, all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, stroke incidence, and serious adverse events
population: Adults with hypertension aged ≥75 years
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether intensive systolic blood pressure control targeting <130 mmHg provides superior cardiovascular and mortality benefits compared with less intensive blood pressure targets (≥130 mmHg) in adults with hypertension aged 75 years or older, without increasing the risk of serious adverse events.

comparison: Usual care (physician-only care)
intervention: Patient care teams comprising multidisciplinary healthcare providers (physicians, nurses, pharmacists, physician assistants, dieticians, social workers, and community health workers) with physician involvement
outcome: Office systolic blood pressure reduction and risk of uncontrolled blood pressure
population: Patients with hypertension
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates whether patient care teams involving physicians are effective in improving blood pressure control in patients with hypertension compared to usual care, as measured by changes in office systolic blood pressure and the risk of uncontrolled blood pressure.

comparison: Usual care
intervention: Self-measurement of blood pressure at home (home BP measurement, HBPM) using a cuff device
outcome: Systolic and diastolic blood pressure changes, number of antihypertensive medications, body mass index changes, and risk of severe adverse outcomes
population: Patients with hypertension
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether self-measurement of blood pressure at home (home BP measurement, HBPM) using a cuff device reduces blood pressure levels in patients with hypertension compared to usual care, and examines whether co-interventions such as telemonitoring enhance this effect.

comparison: Control group (usual care or conventional lifestyle interventions)
intervention: Digital therapeutics (DTx) intervention
outcome: Systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, blood pressure control rate, body mass index, weight, waist circumference, and physical activity
population: Adults with hypertension
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether digital therapeutics (DTx) intervention improves blood pressure management and related health outcomes in adults with hypertension compared to control groups receiving usual care or conventional interventions.

comparison: Control conditions without behavioural interventions
intervention: Behavioural interventions including consumption feedback, social comparison messages, choice architecture (nudges), and tailored environmental appeals
outcome: Factual changes in climate change mitigation behaviours including energy consumption, transportation choices, animal product consumption, food waste, water consumption, and recycling
population: Individuals and households in real-world settings
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether behavioural interventions (such as consumption feedback, social comparison messages, choice architecture/nudges, and tailored environmental appeals) are effective in promoting climate change mitigation behaviours among individuals and households compared to control conditions, measuring actual behavioural changes in energy consumption, transportation, animal product consumption, food waste, water consumption, and recycling.

comparison: High fauna treatments (contiguous and/or protected forests with intact faunal communities, or open controls in exclosure experiments)
exposure: Vertebrate defaunation caused by hunting and habitat fragmentation, including loss of primates, birds, and other vertebrate species
outcome: Forest regeneration measures including density or richness of regenerating tree community, density or dispersion of individual tree species, woody vegetation cover, and biomass
population: Forest ecosystems (41 forest landscapes in 27 countries) with woody vegetation including regenerating tree seedlings and saplings
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the direction and magnitude of vertebrate defaunation impacts on natural forest regeneration globally, examining whether the loss of vertebrates due to hunting and habitat fragmentation affects woody vegetation outcomes such as tree seedling density, species richness, and biomass compared to forests with intact faunal communities.

comparison: Populations with reduced or absent sexual selection (e.g., enforced monogamy or removal of mate competition)
intervention: Experimental manipulation of the presence or intensity of sexual selection on males
outcome: Population fitness components including lifespan, reproductive success, population extinction rate, mutation load, proportion of viable offspring, and phenotypic variance of fitness-related traits
population: Captive populations of various species used in experimental evolution studies
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether sexual selection on males improves population fitness in experimental evolution studies, examining how manipulating the presence or intensity of sexual selection affects fitness components such as survival, reproductive success, extinction rate, and mutation load across different environmental conditions.

comparison: Plant monocultures
exposure: Plant species diversity (plant mixtures with varying species richness)
outcome: Microbial biomass (total, bacterial, fungal), fungi:bacteria ratio, Gram-positive to Gram-negative bacteria ratio, microbial C:N ratio, microbial respiration, and metabolic quotient
population: Soil microbial communities in global terrestrial ecosystems including natural forests, planted forests, planted grasslands, croplands, and planted containers
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates how plant species diversity affects soil microorganisms, specifically examining whether plant mixtures compared to monocultures influence microbial biomass (total, bacterial, and fungal), fungi:bacteria ratio, Gram-positive to Gram-negative bacteria ratio, microbial C:N ratio, respiration, and metabolic quotient across global terrestrial ecosystems.

comparison: Baseline climatological conditions and periods without marine heatwave occurrence
exposure: Large-scale climate modes (e.g., ENSO), teleconnection processes, local physical processes (ocean advective fluxes, air-sea heat fluxes, mixed layer dynamics)
outcome: Marine heatwave occurrence, frequency, intensity, and duration as measured by sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding defined thresholds
population: Global ocean regions and marine environments from 1950 to 2016
research_question: This systematic review provides a global assessment of marine heatwaves (MHWs) to identify the important local processes, large-scale climate modes, and teleconnections that drive and modulate MHW occurrences across different ocean regions, examining how these extreme temperature events relate to modes of climate variability and the physical conditions causing ocean warming above threshold levels.

comparison: Female sex
exposure: Male sex
outcome: SARS-CoV-2 infection proportion, intensive treatment unit (ITU) admission, and death
population: Patients with confirmed COVID-19 infection worldwide
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether male sex is a risk factor for severe COVID-19 outcomes, specifically examining if there are differences between males and females in the proportion of confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infections, the odds of requiring intensive treatment unit (ITU) admission, and the odds of death.

comparison: Passive control conditions and active control conditions
intervention: Social comparison as a behaviour change technique (SC-BCT)
outcome: Behavioural outcomes related to climate change mitigation, health behaviours, performance, and service behaviours measured in short-term (mean 3.7 months) and long-term (mean 6.2 months) post-intervention
population: General population across various behavioural domains including climate change mitigation, health, performance, and service contexts
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates how effective social comparison as a behaviour change technique (SC-BCT) is when applied as the primary intervention or when added to a behaviour change technique bundle, examining its effects on behaviours related to climate change mitigation, health, performance, and service outcomes compared to passive and active control conditions.

comparison: Transient elastography as reference test (liver stiffness measurement thresholds at 7.9 kPa for significant fibrosis and 12.2 kPa for cirrhosis)
exposure: Non-invasive fibrosis biomarkers (APRI, FIB-4, and GPR) at various diagnostic thresholds
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) for detecting significant liver fibrosis and cirrhosis
population: Chronic hepatitis B patients living in sub-Saharan Africa
research_question: This individual-patient-data meta-analysis evaluates the diagnostic performance of non-invasive fibrosis biomarkers (APRI, FIB-4, and GPR) for detecting significant liver fibrosis and cirrhosis in chronic hepatitis B patients living in sub-Saharan Africa, using transient elastography as the reference standard, to determine whether WHO-recommended thresholds are appropriate for this population.

comparison: Gammaretroviral vector (γRV) versus lentiviral vector (LV) platforms; self-inactivating γRV as additional comparator
intervention: Ex-vivo gene therapy with hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) transduced with integrating viral vectors (gammaretroviral vectors or lentiviral vectors)
outcome: Survival (death incidence rate), genotoxicity (insertional mutagenesis events), and engraftment rate of gene-corrected cells
population: Patients with monogenic disorders including primary immunodeficiencies, metabolic diseases, haemoglobinopathies, and bone marrow failures
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to assess the short and long-term safety and efficacy of ex-vivo gene therapy with hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) engineered with integrating vectors for treating monogenic disorders, comparing outcomes between gammaretroviral vectors and lentiviral vectors in terms of survival, genotoxicity, and engraftment of gene-corrected cells.

comparison: Different methodological parameters compared across studies (varying filter types, sampling volumes, storage conditions, and analytical approaches)
exposure: Various filter-based aerosol sampling parameters including sampling volume, filter type, storage conditions, and molecular diagnostic methods for SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection
outcome: Detection positivity rate, quantification of SARS-CoV-2 genetic material (RNA), and viral viability in aerosol samples
population: Aerosol samples collected from indoor and outdoor environments potentially containing SARS-CoV-2, including healthcare settings and areas near infected individuals
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines how sampling and analytical parameters (including sampling volume, filter type, storage conditions, and molecular diagnostic methods) affect the detection positivity rate, quantification, and characterization of airborne SARS-CoV-2 RNA in aerosols collected using filter-based approaches in both indoor and outdoor environments.

comparison: Carbon pricing policies without revenue recycling options (or public finance as baseline in meta-regression)
intervention: Introduction of revenue recycling options (green spending, uniform cash transfers, tax reductions, targeted transfers) alongside carbon pricing policies
outcome: Change in public support for carbon pricing policies (measured as difference in support levels before and after presenting revenue recycling options)
population: General public survey respondents across 26 countries (over 100,000 respondents total)
research_question: This meta-analysis examines how the introduction of revenue recycling options (such as green spending, uniform cash transfers, tax reductions, or targeted transfers) affects public support for direct and indirect carbon pricing policies compared to carbon pricing policies without revenue recycling, based on survey data from the general public across multiple countries.

comparison: Histopathological tumor size measurement (gold standard)
exposure: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) tumor size measurement, including dynamic contrast enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI)
outcome: Accuracy of tumor size prediction (mean difference between MRI and pathology measurements, concordance rates, accuracy rates)
population: Women with histopathology-proven pure ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) of the breast
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in measuring the size of pure ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) compared to histopathological measurements, to better understand the role of MRI in preoperative planning and clinical management of this intraductal breast neoplasm.

comparison: Normal-weight patients (BMI <25 kg/m²)
exposure: Overweight status (body mass index ≥25 kg/m² at time of TNBC diagnosis)
outcome: Disease-free survival and overall survival (measured as hazard ratios)
population: Patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether overweight (BMI ≥25 kg/m²) is associated with poorer prognosis, specifically shorter disease-free survival and overall survival, in patients with triple-negative breast cancer compared to normal-weight patients.

comparison: Platinum-free chemotherapy regimens (standard anthracyclines and taxanes-based regimens)
intervention: Platinum-based chemotherapy regimens (including carboplatin or cisplatin, either added to standard anthracyclines and taxanes regimens or combined with taxanes alone)
outcome: Overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS)
population: Patients with early stage triple negative breast cancer (eTNBC)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether platinum-based chemotherapy regimens improve survival outcomes (disease-free survival and overall survival) in patients with early stage triple negative breast cancer compared to platinum-free chemotherapy regimens.

comparison: Standard chemotherapy, PARPi monotherapy versus PARPi combined with platinum-based chemotherapy, and subgroup comparisons based on BRCA1 versus BRCA2 mutations and prior platinum exposure
intervention: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors (olaparib, rucaparib, niraparib, talazoparib, veliparib) as monotherapy or in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy
outcome: Objective response rate (ORR), clinical benefit rate (CBR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS)
population: Patients with metastatic breast cancer, predominantly with BRCA mutations
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the efficacy of PARP inhibitors (PARPi) in patients with metastatic breast cancer, examining whether certain subgroups (based on BRCA mutation status, receptor status, prior platinum exposure, and combination with platinum-based chemotherapy) derive greater benefit from treatment, as measured by objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, progression-free survival, and overall survival.

comparison: Direct effects of experienced/perceived weight stigma on outcomes without the mediating pathway through internalised weight stigma
exposure: Experienced/perceived weight stigma
outcome: Biopsychosocial outcomes including disordered eating, body shame, body dissatisfaction, exercise behaviour, healthcare experiences and behaviours, bodily pain, parental weight talk, depression, and anxiety
population: Individuals who have experienced or perceived weight stigma (primarily those with overweight/obesity)
research_question: This systematic review examines whether internalised weight stigma mediates the relationship between experienced/perceived weight stigma and biopsychosocial outcomes (including psychological, behavioral, and physical health outcomes) in individuals who have experienced weight-based stigmatization.

comparison: No intervention or evidence-based lifestyle interventions delivered through direct human effort
intervention: Automated digital lifestyle interventions (delivered via mobile application, telephone, or other electronic means without significant human effort)
outcome: Weight loss (percentage weight loss from baseline)
population: Adults with overweight or obesity
research_question: This systematic review examines whether automated digital lifestyle interventions delivered via mobile applications, telephone, or other electronic means without significant human effort can effectively promote weight loss in adults with overweight or obesity compared to no intervention or evidence-based interventions delivered through direct human contact.

comparison: Body mass index (BMI) as the reference standard for obesity measurement
exposure: Body composition measurement indicators including body fat percentage (%BF), fat mass (FM), waist circumference (WC), and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR)
outcome: Correlation coefficients and measurement consistency (agreement) between body composition indicators and BMI for obesity classification
population: Children and adolescents (pre-adolescence and adolescence)
research_question: This systematic review evaluates the correlation and consistency between body composition measurement indicators (such as body fat percentage, fat mass, waist circumference, and waist-to-height ratio) and body mass index (BMI) for assessing overweight and obesity in children and adolescents.

comparison: Pre-intervention baseline values (within-group comparison) and comparison among the three intervention types (CR vs EX vs CREX)
intervention: Weight loss induced by calorie restriction (CR), exercise (EX), or combined calorie restriction and exercise (CREX)
outcome: Fasting circulating concentrations of appetite-related gut hormones including total ghrelin, acylated ghrelin, total PYY, PYY3-36, total GLP-1, active GLP-1, and cholecystokinin (CCK)
population: Adults with overweight or obesity
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates how weight loss achieved through calorie restriction, exercise, or a combination of both affects fasting circulating concentrations of appetite-related gut hormones (ghrelin, PYY, GLP-1, and CCK) in people with overweight or obesity, and whether hormonal responses differ among these three intervention approaches.

comparison: Control groups without school environment interventions (standard school conditions)
intervention: School environment interventions modifying food provision (e.g., food availability, marketing, labeling) and built environment (e.g., school premises modifications, materials for physical activity)
outcome: Obesity-related measurements including BMI, overweight prevalence, and obesity rates
population: School-age children and adolescents in Latin America and the Caribbean
research_question: This systematic review examines whether school environment interventions and policies targeting food provision and built environments are effective in preventing or reducing overweight and obesity among school-age children in Latin America and the Caribbean compared to control groups without such interventions.

comparison: Individuals with healthy body weight (BMI < 25 kg/m²) and normal waist circumference
exposure: Degree and duration of overweight and obesity, measured by body mass index (BMI) and waist circumference (WC) assessed at two time points before the pandemic
outcome: SARS-CoV-2 infection (defined by positive PCR or rapid-antigen test, physician-ascertained COVID-19, or serology)
population: Dutch adults from nine population-based prospective cohort studies (99,570 participants)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether the degree and duration of overweight and obesity (including abdominal obesity measured by waist circumference) are associated with increased risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection among Dutch adults compared to individuals with healthy body weight.

comparison: Control group without exercise intervention
intervention: Exercise interventions (varying in intensity, duration, and session length)
outcome: Adipokine levels (adiponectin, leptin, resistin, and visfatin)
population: Overweight and obese children and adolescents aged 6-18 years
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether exercise interventions are effective in modifying adipokine levels (adiponectin, leptin, resistin, and visfatin) in children and adolescents aged 6-18 years with obesity compared to control groups without exercise intervention.

comparison: Uni-modal AI-assisted screening methods and healthy controls
exposure: AI-assisted multi-modal physiological and behavioral information methods (EEG, eye movement, facial expressions, speech, and gait analysis) using machine learning and deep learning algorithms
outcome: Classification performance measured by AUC (Area Under the Curve) for depression screening accuracy
population: Individuals undergoing depression screening (including depression patients and healthy controls)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether AI-assisted multi-modal physiological and behavioral information (including EEG, eye movement, video/audio monitoring, and gait analysis) can improve classification performance for depression screening compared to uni-modal methods, and evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of these approaches in identifying individuals with depression.

comparison: Standard reference methods (immunohistochemistry targeting mismatch repair proteins and/or polymerase chain reaction assays)
exposure: Deep learning algorithm-based analysis of hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole slide images
outcome: Diagnostic performance metrics including sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve for MSI-H detection
population: Colorectal cancer patients with tissue samples analyzed via whole slide images
research_question: This meta-analysis evaluates the diagnostic performance of deep learning algorithms using whole slide images (WSIs) for detecting microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) status in colorectal cancer patients, compared to standard reference methods such as immunohistochemistry and polymerase chain reaction assays.

comparison: Control groups (standard care or usual care without mHealth intervention)
intervention: Mobile health (mHealth) interventions including text messaging and mobile applications for blood pressure self-management, often incorporating lifestyle advice, self-monitoring equipment, and digital device training
outcome: Systolic blood pressure (SBP) reduction at 6 months
population: Urban populations with digital health disparities in high-income countries, including older adults (≥65 years), individuals with lower educational attainment (≤high school education), and racial/ethnic minorities with hypertension
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether mobile health (mHealth) interventions, including text messaging and mobile applications, are effective for blood pressure self-management in urban populations with digital health disparities, specifically older adults (≥65 years), individuals with lower educational attainment, and racial/ethnic minorities, compared to control conditions.

comparison: Patient-reported outcome (PRO) questionnaires for fatigue assessment
exposure: Digital and imaging technologies (including wrist-worn wearables and imaging modalities)
outcome: Associations between fatigue (measured by PROs) and digital/imaging endpoints (digital biomarkers)
population: Individuals with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (rheumatoid arthritis, primary Sjögren's syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, and inflammatory bowel disease)
research_question: This systematic review explores how digital and imaging technologies have been used to measure fatigue in individuals with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (including rheumatoid arthritis, primary Sjögren's syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, and inflammatory bowel disease), and determines whether significant associations exist between fatigue assessed by patient-reported outcomes and digital/imaging biomarkers.

comparison: Traditional diagnostic or management approaches (standard care without AI)
intervention: Clinical artificial intelligence interventions including machine learning, deep learning algorithms, and AI-based diagnostic and prognostic tools
outcome: Cost-effectiveness (incremental cost-effectiveness ratios), quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), diagnostic accuracy, budget impact, and resource utilization
population: Patients across diverse healthcare settings including hospitals, primary care, and community-based systems, spanning clinical specialties such as oncology, cardiology, ophthalmology, dentistry, infectious diseases, intensive care, and diagnostic imaging
research_question: This systematic review evaluates the cost-effectiveness, utility, and budget impact of clinical artificial intelligence interventions across diverse healthcare settings and domains, comparing AI-based diagnostic and management approaches to traditional methods in terms of clinical effectiveness and economic outcomes.

comparison: Active sensing data (ecological momentary assessment/EMA surveys) and traditional assessment methods
exposure: Passive sensing data from smartphones and wearables (digital markers including physiological signals, social signals, and behavioral signals such as geolocation and sleep parameters)
outcome: Prediction of suicidal thoughts and behaviors (suicidal ideation, suicide attempts, and deaths by suicide)
population: Individuals at risk for suicidal thoughts and behaviors, including high-risk populations and young people
research_question: This systematic review examines whether passive sensing data collected from smartphones and wearable devices can feasibly and validly predict suicidal thoughts and behaviors in high-risk populations compared to active sensing methods such as ecological momentary assessment.

comparison: Standardized guidelines and best practices for dataset documentation, ethical approval disclosure, and licensing requirements
exposure: Availability and documentation practices of open-source oral-maxillofacial imaging datasets (including ethical clearance disclosure, licensing specifications, and annotation details)
outcome: Dataset characteristics (imaging modalities, image counts, annotation availability, annotator qualifications), ethical approval disclosure rates, and licensing/terms specification rates for dataset reuse
population: Openly accessible oral-maxillofacial imaging datasets containing patient images from dental and maxillofacial sources
research_question: This systematic review aims to identify and characterize openly accessible oral-maxillofacial imaging datasets, examining their characteristics (including imaging modalities, annotations, and sources), ethical approval status, and licensing requirements for reuse in AI research and development.

comparison: Unimodal models using single data modalities
exposure: Multimodal digital pathology techniques combining whole slide images with clinical, genomic, radiological, and other imaging data
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy, survival prediction, and treatment response prediction
population: Patients with colorectal cancer
research_question: This systematic review examines the effectiveness of multimodal digital pathology techniques that integrate whole slide images with other modalities (such as clinical information, genomics data, radiological scans, and MRI) for improving diagnostic accuracy, survival prediction, and treatment planning in patients with colorectal cancer compared to unimodal approaches.

comparison: Traditional healthcare practices without LLM integration or human oversight standards
exposure: Use and deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT in medical and healthcare applications
outcome: Ethical considerations including fairness, bias, non-maleficence, transparency, privacy concerns, production of harmful or inaccurate content, and requirements for ethical guidance and human oversight
population: Medicine and healthcare settings, including clinical practice, medical education, health research, and patient care contexts
research_question: This systematic review aims to identify and map the ethically relevant applications, interventions, and contexts where Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT have been tested or proposed in medicine and healthcare, and to determine the principal ethical outcomes including opportunities, risks, benefits, and potential harms associated with their use in these sectors.

comparison: Control groups (non-exergaming conditions)
intervention: Exergaming interventions (virtual reality-based exergaming and video-based exergaming)
outcome: Cognitive functions including global cognitive function, learning and memory (immediate and delayed recall), working memory, verbal fluency, and executive function
population: People with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia
research_question: This meta-analysis examines whether exergaming interventions improve cognitive functions in people with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia compared to control conditions, and investigates whether the effects vary by type of exergaming (virtual reality-based vs. video-based) and training duration.

comparison: mHealth interventions without social features or control conditions
intervention: Mobile health (mHealth) interventions with integrated social features (e.g., social support, social comparison, online social network components)
outcome: Physical activity outcomes (standardized difference in means), user engagement, retention rates, and user satisfaction with social features
population: Adults and adolescents, including both patients and healthy consumers
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether mobile health (mHealth) interventions incorporating social features (such as social support and social comparison) are effective in promoting physical activity and improving user engagement compared to standard mHealth interventions or control conditions, among both patients and healthy consumers.

comparison: Inconsistent or absent co-design reporting standards and practices across reviews
intervention: Co-design methodologies and approaches used in digital health intervention development
outcome: Co-design methodology characteristics (participant involvement frequency and breadth, session details, co-design strategies), participant evaluation of co-design process, and methodological quality of reporting
population: Patients, caregivers, healthcare professionals, and other end-users involved in digital health intervention co-design
research_question: This umbrella review aims to synthesize what is known about the practical methods used to conduct co-design of digital health interventions, including setting, population, intervention details, session length, co-design strategies, and the breadth and depth of end-user involvement in the co-design process.

comparison: Studies without wearable device integration or standard care without continuous physiological monitoring
exposure: Use of wearable devices during and/or after cancer treatment
outcome: Physiological data collection (including physical activity levels, heart rate, sleep patterns, electrocardiograms, respiratory rate, blood oxygen saturation), monitoring of treatment-related side effects, and potential clinical benefits of wearable device utilization
population: Pediatric and young adult patients (aged 0-25 years) with a cancer diagnosis
research_question: This scoping review aims to understand how wearable devices are being utilized in pediatric and young adult oncology patients (aged 0-25 years), what types of physiological data are being collected, and whether there are potential benefits or inefficacies of wearable devices in this population during and/or after cancer treatment.

comparison: Standard diagnostic methods or clinical diagnosis based on DSM-5 and ICD-11 frameworks
exposure: Artificial intelligence-driven diagnostic technologies and models
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and performance metrics of AI models in identifying mental disorders (ranging from 21% to 100% accuracy)
population: Patients with mental disorders including Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, autism spectrum disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, and psychotic disorders
research_question: This umbrella review aims to synthesize the evidence from systematic reviews on the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI) models in identifying mental disorders across various conditions including Alzheimer's disease, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, autism spectrum disorder, and other psychiatric conditions.

comparison: Non-use or limited adoption of digital health technologies
exposure: Use of digital health technologies (including wearable devices, computerized decision support systems, telemedicine, electronic health records, and social media platforms)
outcome: Barriers (infrastructure and technical issues, psychological and personal issues, workload concerns) and facilitators (training/educational programs, multisector incentives, perception of technology effectiveness) to digital health technology adoption
population: Healthcare professionals including physicians, pharmacists, and nurses
research_question: This overview of systematic reviews aims to consolidate and synthesize the evidence on barriers and facilitators that influence healthcare professionals' adoption and utilization of digital health technologies, examining what factors hinder or enable physicians, pharmacists, and nurses from effectively implementing digital interventions in clinical practice.

comparison: Standard care or control conditions without mHealth app intervention
intervention: Stand-alone mHealth apps (mobile health applications that do not require dedicated central servers and additional human resources)
outcome: Health outcomes related to various health conditions managed in general practice settings
population: Patients with various health conditions presenting in general practice
research_question: This overview of systematic reviews aims to identify and evaluate the effectiveness of prescribable stand-alone mHealth apps across different health conditions that present in general practice, and to determine the gaps and limitations in mHealth app research.

comparison: Usual care, standard care, or competing alternative interventions
intervention: Digital health interventions including text-messaging, smartphone applications, and website-based interventions targeting lifestyle modifications for T2DM and hypertension prevention and treatment
outcome: Cost-effectiveness measured by incremental cost-utility ratios (ICUR), quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and costs
population: Adults with or at risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and/or hypertension, including those with prediabetes and prehypertension
research_question: This systematic review synthesizes and compares the cost-effectiveness of digital health interventions, specifically text-messaging, smartphone applications, and website-based interventions, for the prevention and treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and/or hypertension in adults with or at risk of these conditions compared to usual care or alternative interventions.
